fullData.title: Adding on a Number Line Without Regrouping
fullData.subject: Arithmetic

problem.statement: Leo wants to add 24 and 13. He starts at number 24 on the number line and jumps forward by 10, then jumps forward by 3 more. Use the number line to find the final number Leo lands on.

fullData.solutionStrategy: Break the number $13$ into $10$ and $3$ using place value, then find the starting point $24$ on the number line. Make a large jump forward of $+10$ to add the tens, followed by a smaller jump of $+3$ to add the ones without needing to regroup. Reading the tick mark where the final jump lands reveals the sum.

content.imagePrompt: A clean educational number line graphic on a white background, marked from 20 to 40 with evenly spaced tick marks. A prominent purple dot and label points to tick 24 labeled Start@24. Above the number line, text boxes display the place-value breakdown 13 = 10 + 3 in bright blue and orange colors.
content.altText: A number line showing the starting point at 24 and the place value breakdown of 13 into 10 and 3.

labels.description: Leo's starting position on the number line.
Splitting the number 13 into tens and ones.

annotations.steps: I located tick mark 24 on the number line and split the number 13 into 10 and 3.
annotations.strategy: I notice that breaking 13 into tens and ones makes the addition much easier to handle in smaller, sequential chunks rather than all at once.
annotations.misconceptions: Students often make the mistake of counting 24 as a jump instead of starting on it, which leads to an off-by-one error.
annotations.connections: This strategy of breaking numbers apart by place value lays the foundation for mental math and standard addition algorithms.
annotations.narrative: Locate Leo's starting position on the Figure 1 number line at tick $24$, labeled **Start@24**. Leo is adding $13$, which splits by place value into $1\text{ ten}$ and $3\text{ ones}$ ($13 = 10 + 3$). Breaking $13$ into tens and ones allows Leo to add in two clear steps: first jump forward by $10$, then jump forward by $3$.

challenge.prompt: Leo is at 24 on the number line and takes a jump of 10 forward. What number does he land on?
challenge.rationale: Adding 10 increases the tens digit by 1 while leaving the ones digit unchanged, landing on 34 rather than adding to the ones place to get 25.

annotations.steps: Take the starting number 24 and add 10 by moving the tens digit up by one while keeping the ones digit the same, landing on 34.
annotations.strategy: I notice that adding 10 to a two-digit number is much easier if I just change the tens digit by 1 and leave the ones digit alone, so I do that first.
annotations.misconceptions: Students might mistakenly add 10 to the ones digit instead of the tens digit, getting 25 instead of 34.
annotations.connections: This builds foundational base-ten understanding, preparing students for multi-digit addition and place value grouping.
annotations.narrative: Take the first jump forward by $10$ from tick $24$ to add the tens. Adding $1\text{ ten}$ increases the tens digit by $1$ while the ones digit stays unchanged: $24 + 10 = 34$. On Figure 1, this jump follows the arrow to the point labeled **+10@34**, placing Leo at tick $34$.

transitions.operation: add the ones by counting forward

challenge.prompt: From 34, Leo jumps forward 3 more units. What final number does he land on?
challenge.rationale: Starting at 34 and taking 3 jumps of one lands on 37; counting 34 itself as the first jump leads to landing short on 36.

annotations.steps: Take the second jump forward by 3 from tick 34 to add the ones, counting forward 3 individual tick marks 35, 36, and 37 to land on tick 37.
annotations.strategy: I notice that after adding the tens to reach 34, I can just count on by ones to finish adding the remaining 3 units without needing to regroup.
annotations.misconceptions: A common mistake is counting the starting number 34 as the first jump, which leads to landing incorrectly on 36 instead of 37.
annotations.connections: This connects place value decomposition to movement along a number line, reinforcing that addition is simply counting forward in chunks of tens and ones.
annotations.narrative: Take the second jump forward by $3$ from tick $34$ to add the ones. Count forward $3$ individual tick marks on Figure 1: $35$, $36$, and $37$, which gives $34 + 3 = 37$. On Figure 1, this step reaches the point labeled **+3@37**, landing Leo directly on tick $37$.

annotations.steps: I add the ones together (4 + 3 = 7) and the tens together (20 + 10 = 30) separately, then combine the partial sums.
annotations.strategy: I notice that by breaking the numbers into tens and ones, I can add them easily without needing any extra steps or regrouping.
annotations.misconceptions: Students often make mistakes by accidentally adding the tens digit to the ones digit (like 20 + 3), forgetting to keep place values separated.
annotations.connections: This reinforces the foundational place-value concept that multidigit addition can always be split into separate place-value columns.
annotations.narrative:
Verify the result using place-value addition to confirm the sum without regrouping:
- Add the ones: $4\text{ ones} + 3\text{ ones} = 7\text{ ones}$.
- Add the tens: $2\text{ tens} + 1\text{ ten} = 3\text{ tens}$.

Combining $3\text{ tens}$ and $7\text{ ones}$ gives $37$. Because the sum of the ones ($7$) is less than $10$, no regrouping is needed, confirming that the final number Leo lands on is $37$.

Breaking $13$ into tens and ones allows Leo to add in two clear steps: first jump forward by $10$, then jump forward by $3$.
---
Take the first jump forward by $10$ from tick $24$ to add the tens. Adding $1\text{ ten}$ increases the tens digit by $1$ while the ones digit stays unchanged: $24 + 10 = 34$. On Figure 1, this jump follows the arrow to the point labeled **+10@34**, placing Leo at tick $34$.
---
Take the second jump forward by $3$ from tick $34$ to add the ones. Count forward $3$ individual tick marks on Figure 1: $35$, $36$, and $37$, which gives $34 + 3 = 37$. On Figure 1, this step reaches the point labeled **+3@37**, landing Leo directly on tick $37$.
---

- Add the ones: $4\text{ ones} + 3\text{ ones} = 7\text{ ones}$.
- Add the tens: $2\text{ tens} + 1\text{ ten} = 3\text{ tens}$.

Combining $3\text{ tens}$ and $7\text{ ones}$ gives $37$. Because the sum of the ones ($7$) is less than $10$, no regrouping is needed, confirming that the final number Leo lands on is $37$.

specs.title: Locate start on number line
specs.pedagogicalGoal: Teach students to identify the starting position on a number line and partition an addend into tens and ones to plan the sequence of jumps.
specs.seedNotes: Render a number line from 20 to 40 highlighting the tick mark 24 labeled Start@24 and the place-value decomposition $13 = 10 + 3$.

specs.title: Jump forward by ten
specs.pedagogicalGoal: Show that adding 10 to a two-digit number increments the tens digit by 1 while leaving the ones digit unchanged.
specs.seedNotes: Evaluate the first jump $24 + 10 = 34$, highlighting that Leo moves from tick 24 to tick 34 labeled +10@34.

specs.title: Jump forward by three
specs.pedagogicalGoal: Demonstrate counting on by ones from an intermediate value to arrive at the final sum.
specs.seedNotes: Evaluate the second jump $34 + 3 = 37$, counting through ticks 35, 36, and 37 to land on tick 37 labeled +3@37.

specs.title: Verify using place-value addition
specs.pedagogicalGoal: Reinforce that adding without regrouping allows tens and ones to be summed independently to verify the total.
specs.seedNotes: Add the ones $4 + 3 = 7$ and tens $2 + 1 = 3$ to show $(20 + 10) + (4 + 3) = 30 + 7 = 37$, noting no regrouping is needed.
